Kepler's second law: the radius vector sweeps **equal areas in equal times**, so the
area is proportional to the time.
**Step 1 — state the law.** The **areal velocity** dA/dt is **constant** for a planet ✓
**Step 2 — write each area as a rate times a time.**
A₁ swept in 2 days: A₁ = 2k
A₂ swept in 3 days: A₂ = 3k
A₃ swept in 6 days: A₃ = 6k ✓
with k the constant areal velocity.
**Step 3 — eliminate k.**
A₁/2 = A₂/3 = A₃/6 ✓
**Step 4 — clear the denominators.** Multiplying through by 6:
**3A₁ = 2A₂ = A₃** ✓
**A check with numbers.** Take k = 1 unit per day:
A₁ = **2**, A₂ = **3**, A₃ = **6**
3A₁ = **6**, 2A₂ = **6**, A₃ = **6** ✓ all equal.
**Why the areal velocity is constant.** It is **conservation of angular momentum** in
disguise ✓
dA/dt = L/(2m)
and since gravity is a **central** force - always directed at the Sun - it exerts no
torque about the Sun, so L cannot change.
**What the law implies about speed.** Near **perihelion** the planet is close to the Sun,
so it must move **faster** to sweep the same area ✓ At **aphelion** it is far away and
slow. The Earth is fastest in early January, when it is nearest the Sun.
**Why this law needs no knowledge of the orbit's shape.** It follows from the central
nature of the force alone, not from the inverse-square law ✓ Any central force gives
equal areas in equal times; only an inverse-square force gives **ellipses**.
**The other two laws, for context.**
**first**: the orbit is an ellipse with the Sun at one focus
**third**: T² ∝ a³ ✓
**Reading the distractors.** Each alternative sets the areas proportional to the wrong
powers or inverses of the times ✓ The test is simple: A must **grow** with the time, in
direct proportion, so A₃ (6 days) must be three times A₁ (2 days) - which only
3A₁ = A₃ expresses.
∴ 3 A₁ = 2 A₂ = A₃.

Below the surface, g falls **linearly** with depth.
**Step 1 — state the formula.**
g_d = g(1 − d/R) ✓
**Step 2 — substitute.**
g_d = 9·8(1 − 1600/6400)
= 9·8(1 − 0·25)
= 9·8(0·75)
= **7·35 m s⁻²** ✓
**Why g decreases with depth.** At a depth d only the mass **within** the radius
(R − d) attracts the body ✓ By the shell theorem, the shell of material **above** it
exerts **no net force** at all. With a uniform Earth, the enclosed mass goes as
(R − d)³ while the inverse-square gives (R − d)⁻², leaving
g ∝ **(R − d)** - a linear fall.
**Checking the limits.**
at d = 0: g_d = **9·8 m s⁻²** ✓ the surface value
at d = R, the centre: g_d = **0** ✓ with mass pulling equally in all directions.
**The contrast with height.** Above the surface the fall is **quadratic**:
g_h = g/(1 + h/R)² ≈ g(1 − 2h/R) for small h ✓
so at a **height** of 1600 km, g = 9·8(6400/8000)² = **6·27 m s⁻²** - a different
answer, and the reason the question specifies "depth".
**Which falls faster near the surface.** Comparing the two approximations,
depth: g(1 − d/R)
height: g(1 − 2h/R) ✓
so near the surface g falls **twice as fast** going up as going down - rising 1 km costs
twice what descending 1 km does.
**The real Earth.** It is **not** uniform: the dense iron core makes g actually
**increase** slightly with depth down to the core-mantle boundary, peaking near
**10·7 m s⁻²** ✓ The linear formula assumes uniform density, which is the standard
idealisation for this calculation.
**Reading the distractors.** **4·9 m s⁻²** ✗ is g/2, which would need d = R/2 = 3200 km.
**9·8 m s⁻²** ✗ is the surface value unchanged. **19·6 m s⁻²** ✗ is **twice** g, and
nothing can make g increase in this model ✓
∴ 7.35 ms⁻².

Contracting the Earth conserves **angular momentum**, so it spins faster and the day
shortens.
**Step 1 — state the conservation law.** No external torque acts on the contracting
Earth, so
I₁ω₁ = I₂ω₂ ✓
**Step 2 — write the moment of inertia.** For a uniform sphere,
I = (2/5)MR², so **I ∝ R²** ✓ with the mass unchanged.
**Step 3 — see what halving R does.**
I₂ = I₁/4 ✓
so, to keep Iω constant,
ω₂ = **4ω₁**
**Step 4 — convert to the period.** T = 2π/ω, so
T₂ = T₁/4
= 24/4
= **6 hours** ✓
**Why T ∝ R².** Combining the two steps, T ∝ 1/ω ∝ I ∝ R² ✓ so halving the radius
quarters the day, and the factor is a **square**, not a simple proportion.
**The everyday analogy.** A spinning skater pulls in her arms and speeds up ✓ Her moment
of inertia falls, and since nothing exerts a torque on her, her angular velocity must
rise to compensate - exactly the same physics.
**Where the extra energy comes from.** The rotational kinetic energy is
E = ½Iω² = **L²/(2I)** ✓
With L fixed and I quartered, the energy **quadruples**. The work is done by the
gravitational forces performing the contraction - the Earth would have to give up
gravitational potential energy to shrink.
**The astrophysical case.** This is precisely why **neutron stars** spin so fast ✓ A
star of the Sun's size rotating once a month collapses to a radius of about 10 km, and
the (R₁/R₂)² factor of some 10¹⁰ turns a monthly rotation into one of **milliseconds** -
the observed pulsars.
**Why the mass is assumed constant.** The question says the Earth **contracts**, not
that it loses material ✓ With M fixed, only R enters.
**Reading the distractors.** **24 h** ✗ assumes no change. **18 h** ✗ and **30 h** ✗
correspond to no factor arising from R² ✓ The answer must be a **quarter** of 24, and
only 6 h is.
∴ 6 h.

For an ideal gas at a fixed temperature, **PV is constant** - so a plot of PV against V
is a horizontal line.
**Step 1 — state the gas law.**
PV = nRT ✓
**Step 2 — see what is plotted.** The vertical axis is **PV** and the horizontal axis
is **V**. At constant temperature the right-hand side nRT does not change, so
**PV = constant**, independent of V ✓
**Step 3 — identify the graph.** A constant value plotted against V is a **horizontal
straight line** - the second graph ✓
**Why this is the test for ideality.** A **real** gas obeys PV = nRT only approximately ✓
Plotting PV against P or V reveals the deviations at once: the line **sags** at moderate
pressures, where attractive forces dominate, and **rises** at high pressures, where the
molecules' own volume matters. A perfectly horizontal line is the signature of an
**ideal** gas.
**What van der Waals adds.**
(P + a/V²)(V − b) = RT ✓
the **a** term for intermolecular attraction, the **b** term for molecular volume. Set
both to zero and the horizontal line is recovered.
**Why the other graphs are wrong.**
a **rising straight line** ✗ would mean PV ∝ V, that is P constant - an isobaric
process, not an isothermal one
a **falling straight line** ✗ would mean PV decreasing as the gas expands, so the
temperature would be dropping
a **hyperbola** ✗ is what **P against V** looks like for an isotherm, not PV against
V ✓ That last is the most tempting error, since the hyperbola is the familiar
isothermal curve.
**The distinction worth fixing.**
**P against V** at constant T: a **hyperbola**, P = nRT/V ✓
**PV against V** at constant T: a **horizontal line** ✓
Reading which quantity is on the vertical axis is the whole of this question.
**When would the line not be horizontal?** If the temperature changed during the
process ✓ Along an **adiabatic** curve, for instance, PV falls as the gas expands and
cools.
∴ the horizontal line.

The net work in a cycle is the **area enclosed**, with a sign set by the **direction**
round the loop.
**Step 1 — read the three vertices.**
A: (V₁, P₁)
B: (3V₁, P₁)
C: (V₁, 4P₁) ✓
**Step 2 — find the enclosed area.** The triangle has
base: 3V₁ − V₁ = **2V₁** (along AB)
height: 4P₁ − P₁ = **3P₁** (from A up to C)
area = ½(2V₁)(3P₁)
= **3P₁V₁** ✓
**Step 3 — find the sign.** Trace A → B → C → A:
A to B: rightwards along the bottom
B to C: up and to the left
C to A: straight down ✓
That circuit runs **anticlockwise**, and an anticlockwise cycle on a P-V diagram does
**negative** net work:
**W = −3P₁V₁** ✓
**Why the direction decides the sign.** Work is ∫P dV, positive when the gas **expands**
and negative when it is **compressed** ✓ Going round anticlockwise, the compression
happens at the **higher** pressures and the expansion at the lower, so the negative
contribution wins.
**Checking stage by stage.**
**A to B**, expansion at constant P₁: W = P₁(2V₁) = **+2P₁V₁**
**B to C**, a straight line from (3V₁, P₁) to (V₁, 4P₁): the gas is compressed by 2V₁ at
an average pressure of 2·5P₁, so W = **−5P₁V₁**
**C to A**, at constant volume: W = **0**
total: 2 − 5 + 0 = **−3P₁V₁** ✓ exactly the enclosed area, with sign.
**What the sign means physically.** Net **negative** work by the gas means work is done
**on** it over the cycle ✓ This is a **refrigerator or heat pump** cycle, not an engine;
the gas absorbs work and rejects heat.
**The clockwise case.** Reversing the circuit to A → C → B → A would give **+3P₁V₁** -
an engine, delivering useful work ✓ The same area, the opposite sign.
**Why the internal energy change is zero.** The cycle returns to its starting point, so
ΔU = 0 and by the first law **Q = W = −3P₁V₁** ✓ the gas gives out 3P₁V₁ of heat over
the cycle.
∴ −3P₁V₁.

For an ideal gas the internal energy depends on the **temperature alone**, so read the
temperatures off the graph.
**Step 1 — recall the rule.**
U = (f/2)nRT ✓
with f the number of degrees of freedom. No pressure or volume appears - only T.
**Step 2 — read the graph.** The plot is **volume against temperature**. From the
figure, **A and B lie at the same temperature**, with A at the larger volume; **C** is
at a higher temperature than B, at the same volume as B ✓
**Step 3 — compare the internal energies.** Since A and B share a temperature,
**U_A = U_B** ✓
**Step 4 — test the other statements.**
"**at C less than at B**" ✗ - C is at a **higher** temperature, so U_C > U_B.
"**at B more than at A**" ✗ and "**at A more than at B**" ✗ - both are at the same
temperature, so neither is greater ✓
**Why volume does not matter.** For an **ideal** gas there are no intermolecular forces,
so no potential energy is stored in the separation of the molecules ✓ All the internal
energy is kinetic, and the mean kinetic energy per molecule is (3/2)kT - a function of
temperature only. Expanding the gas at constant T changes nothing.
**What is different between A and B.** Their **volumes**, and therefore their
**pressures**: with PV = nRT and T common, the larger volume at A means the **lower**
pressure ✓ Pressure and volume differ; energy does not.
**The contrast with a real gas.** There, attractive forces mean the energy **does**
depend slightly on volume ✓ which is why a real gas cools on free expansion - the
Joule-Thomson effect - while an ideal one does not.
**How the process A to B is described.** Same temperature, different volume - an
**isothermal** change ✓ for which ΔU = 0 and all the heat absorbed becomes work done.
**The energy at C.** Higher temperature means higher internal energy, so the order is
U_C > U_A = U_B ✓
∴ at A and B are equal.

With equal momenta, kinetic energy is **inversely proportional to mass**.
**Step 1 — express the kinetic energy through momentum.**
KE = ½mv² and p = mv, so
**KE = p²/(2m)** ✓
**Step 2 — take the ratio with p common.**
KE₁/KE₂ = m₂/m₁
= 2/1
= **2 : 1** ✓
**Why the lighter body carries more energy.** To have the same momentum it must move
**faster**, and kinetic energy depends on the **square** of the speed while momentum
depends on it only linearly ✓ The extra speed counts twice over.
**A worked check.** Take p = 2 kg m s⁻¹ for both:
1 kg body: v = 2 m s⁻¹, KE = ½(1)(4) = **2 J**
2 kg body: v = 1 m s⁻¹, KE = ½(2)(1) = **1 J** ✓
ratio **2 : 1** ✓
**Where this matters in practice.** It is why a **rifle recoils gently** while its bullet
is lethal ✓ Rifle and bullet carry equal and opposite momentum, but the bullet, being
perhaps a thousand times lighter, takes a thousand times the kinetic energy. The same
principle governs rocket exhaust and the fragments of a nuclear decay.
**The companion question.** If instead the two had **equal kinetic energies**, their
momenta would go as
p = √(2mKE), so **p ∝ √m** ✓
giving p₁ : p₂ = 1 : √2. The heavier body would then carry the **greater** momentum -
the relationship reverses.
**A summary of the two cases.**
equal **momentum** → KE ∝ **1/m**, the lighter body has more energy ✓
equal **energy** → p ∝ **√m**, the heavier body has more momentum ✓
**Reading the distractors.** **1 : 2** ✗ inverts the ratio - it would make the heavier
body the more energetic. **1 : 1** ✗ would need equal masses. **3 : 1** ✗ matches no
mass ratio here ✓
∴ 2 : 1.
